title: Aerodynamic Performance Enhancement of a Double-Row J-Shaped Vertical Axis Wind Turbine Through Angular Phase Optimization
content: The aerodynamic performance of double-row vertical-axis wind turbines (VAWTs) is strongly influenced by the relative angular position of the two blade rows, which governs the flow interaction, wake development, and torque generation. This study presents a three-dimensional numerical investigation into the influence of angular phase difference on the aerodynamic performance of a double-row vertical-axis wind turbine equipped with J-shaped blades. Based on the optimum radial spacing identified in a previous investigation, the outer-to-inner radius ratio was fixed at 1.8, and only the angular phase difference between the two blade rows was varied. The numerical model was validated against available experimental and numerical data to ensure the accuracy of the computational methodology. The aerodynamic performance of the turbine was evaluated through instantaneous and average torque coefficients, while the underlying flow mechanisms were analyzed using velocity, pressure, and vorticity distributions. The results demonstrate that the angular phase difference significantly alters the aerodynamic interaction between the two rotor rows by modifying the synchronization of blade loading and reducing adverse wake interference. Among the investigated configurations, a phase difference of 90° produced the highest aerodynamic performance, yielding an approximately 14.8% increase in the average torque coefficient compared with the corresponding single-row turbine. The improved performance is primarily attributed to a more uniform torque distribution, enhanced flow recovery between the blade rows, and weaker vortex interactions. The findings highlight the importance of angular phase optimization in the aerodynamic design of double-row J-shaped vertical-axis wind turbines and provide practical guidelines for improving their energy conversion efficiency.
